title: Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers
main_claim: Theorem 1.1, the full Hindman finite sums and products conjecture: for every finite coloring of N and every m, there is a set {a_1<...<a_m} with FS∪FP monochromatic. The elements also satisfy the separation a_d > R(sum_{k<d}a_k + prod_{k<d}a_k)^D. The theorem is derived from a Prediction Principle (piecewise-nilsequence dense models of the weighted color indicators) and an Alignment Principle (a choice from a finite list of rational scale vectors with probability >= delta, uniform in model complexity).
coverage: Checked line by line: Section 2 in full. This covers the admissible-parameter conventions, the chain selection Lemma 2.x (Ramsey by cardinality plus Folkman–Rado–Sanders with q_d=2u_d, nonempty tails, index budget <= 2F) and the order of parameters (s(m), then n(m,r), then the lists and delta, then tau, then eta, then Prediction). It also covers the tolerance arithmetic (3C tau, C eta < delta/4, K eta < delta tau^{2^m}/4), the match between the alignment offsets and L_J(z(t)) via B_k in E_{B_d}, the calibration giving S_d(t_{B_d})>2tau from the singleton masks, positivity of the weighted count implying an actual configuration (integrality of c_k/c_d and the zero extension of f), the separation bound through V_e, and Corollaries 1.2 and 2.x. Read the argument of: Section 8 in full. This includes the finite word plan (backward budgets, the inflation identity w[b kappa(k)]=I_k(w)[b], positivity of lambda_e, and compactness of the nilpotent polynomial recurrence in the free step-s group), the residue/progression identity t(p+m r_e)+mM Delta_e = tp + m q_e, conditional face invariance, and the conditional-mass Lemma. The mass Lemma uses the closed sets F_o, Portmanteau, and a loss of exactly 1/Q_i; the slot TV shift then loses 1/V_i. Section 7: the local cube law, the face-lift Proposition (affine map, graded identity from the (i+1)-cube test, shear lift) and shear-haar (class <= s, TV invariance of the weighted boxes). Section 5: the final assembly, i.e. the calibration via psi(S) and <S,psi(S)> <= 3tau, and the telescoping rho->F->S. Only skimmed: the proof of the rough-step Proposition in Section 6 (I tried simple torus counterexamples with phases gamma(t)x; none worked, because t is coprime to W and the denominators exceed w), and the transference and correlation machinery in Sections 3–5 (Lemmas on master scales, prime insertion, mask removal, dense model, energy selection, subgroup inverse). I found no concrete failure, but given the length (about 5,300 lines) and depth, these internals are not certified.
